Subject: Initial proposal: 3-year annualized commitment with stepped ramp

Hi Samir / Karen —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, we modeled a 3-year annualized prepay that gives Acme the ability to lock unit economics up front while protecting against seasonal usage spikes via a defined ramp into year two/three.

High-level proposal (attached):
- Term: 36 months (annualized prepay collected up front each contract year).
- Year 1 actual consumption credit applied monthly against prepay; year 2/3 carry-forward true-up at quarter end.
- Discount profile: 22% base off list for a straight 3-year annualized prepay, with a +3% accelerator (25% total) if commit hits the Year 1 baseline and we agree a capped true-up window.
- Ramp: conservative billing schedule (60% baseline year 1, 80% year 2, 100% year 3 expected throughput) — we included breakpoints and true-up triggers in the spreadsheet.

Attached: ACME_SOW_v3.pdf and acme-pricing-3yr-model.xlsx. Please review and flag anything that feels off. If you want, Jordan can schedule a short call to walk through the model.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm the Year 1 baseline number and whether Acme prefers a quarterly or semi-annual true-up cadence.
2) Once baseline is confirmed, we’ll finalize the SOW and DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachments: ACME_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF), acme-pricing-3yr-model.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Initial proposal: 3-year annualized commitment with stepped ramp

Hi Kim / Vivek —

Forwarding Jordan’s proposal to Acme. They asked if we can do the 25% total discount (22% base + 3% accelerator) and want the accelerator guaranteed if they hit a Year 1 baseline that we both sign off on.

Quick ask: can finance approve a 25% effective discount for this 3-year annualized prepay if we include a 90-day true-up window and a 6-month clawback for over-usage beyond the ramp profile?

Rationale to approve:
- ACME is a strategic logo for the platform team in vertical X; potential to expand Dedicated capacity next 12–18 months.
- Upfront cash improves our revenue visibility and reduces churn risk for the first 12 months.

If you prefer, I can tighten the ramp breakpoints (move Year 1 baseline up 5 percentage points) or add a modest per-token surcharge for overage months to reduce downside.

Appreciate a quick pointer on approvals and any required legal/terms exceptions.

—Olga
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: acme-pricing-3yr-model.xlsx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial proposal: 3-year annualized commitment with stepped ramp

Olga / Jordan —

Thanks for the context. Finance reviewed the model — we can entertain an economic at the 25% headline if the commercial terms address our risk exposure. Proposed guardrails:

1) 25% accelerator becomes payable only after a signed baseline and an executed mid-year true-up (90 days) confirming Year 1 reached >= baseline.
2) Include a 6-month clawback that prorates the accelerator if actual rolling 12-month usage falls >15% below the expected ramp at any true-up point.
3) Add a modest 1.5% per-token overage surcharge on months that exceed the Year 3 projected monthly throughput (applies only after the true-up window).
4) Legal to run the exception: attach a short terms exception doc (redwood-terms-exception.docx).

If Acme agrees to (1)-(3) we will sign off and push the DocuSign. Otherwise, alternate approved path is 22% firm discount with standard true-up and no accelerator.

Kimberly Park
Director, Finance — Revenue & Pricing | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-terms-exception.docx

- Legal to add a 30-day cure period before any clawback is charged.

Olga/Jordan — proceed to finalize the SOW and envelope. Jordan, please include the accelerator language exactly as Kimberly wrote and ensure the DocuSign references the specific true-up dates.

Subject: Final SOW & next steps — ACME 3-year annualized prepay (conditional accelerator)

Hi Samir / Karen —

Thanks for your patience. Per our internal approvals we can offer the 25% headline discount on a conditional basis. Summary of the final terms:

- Term: 36 months, annualized prepay for each contract year.
- Pricing: 22% base discount off list; 3% accelerator (25% total) becomes effective if Acme signs the baseline and hits the Year 1 baseline in the 90-day true-up after Year 1.
- Ramp & breakpoints: Year 1 baseline set to the attached spreadsheet (row "Y1 baseline"), 60% Year 1 / 80% Year 2 / 100% Year 3 expected.
- Clawback: 6-month prorated clawback applicable to accelerator if rolling 12-month usage is >15% below ramp at any true-up point; 30-day cure window before charges.
- Overage: 1.5% per-token surcharge for months that exceed Year 3 projected monthly throughput (applies after true-up).

I’ve attached the updated SOW (ACME_SOW_v3.pdf) and the pricing model (acme-pricing-3yr-model.xlsx). Also attached the terms exception template redwood-terms-exception.docx that Kimberly requested.

If these read OK, please reply with approval to proceed and we’ll send the DocuSign envelope for execution. We can also set up a 30-minute call Monday to go through final questions.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
